caption: Products & Services
vo: Where do the rates, the checklists and the website copy come from? One place. The Products and Services catalogue, with a single sheet for every product.

caption: Sign in as Priya Ramdin — Relationship Manager
vo: Let's start with Priya Ramdin, a relationship manager. She looks products up while she's talking to clients.

caption: Products & Services is the first module under Client 360
vo: Products and Services is the first module under Client 360. It holds twenty-two products and services across six Genesis legal entities.

caption: Each row is one product: code, name, business unit, category, risk rating and "Rate from"
vo: Each row is one product, with its code, name, business unit, category, risk rating and Rate from. The business unit tells you which legal entity provides it.

caption: Filter by legal entity: type part of its name in the search box
vo: Want one entity's products? Just type part of its name in the search box. Here, Genesis Global Funds.

caption: Six investment funds are provided by Genesis Global Funds
vo: And there they are, six investment funds. Search matches what the table shows, not only the codes.

caption: Genesis Life Ltd provides the four loans
vo: Switch to Genesis Life Ltd, and you get the four loans. Real Estate, Personal, Investment-Backed and Commercial.

caption: Open Real Estate Loan to see its product sheet
vo: Let's open the Real Estate Loan.

caption: Details: code, French name, business unit and the legal entity that provides it
vo: The details come first. Code, French name, business unit, and who provides it. Here, Genesis Life Ltd, for the loans business line.

caption: Terms: the margin over the Genesis PLR, maximum tenure, age at maturity and financing (LTV)
vo: Then the terms. The margin over the Genesis PLR, the maximum tenure, the age at maturity and the LTV. Loan applications check these limits, and take the margin for pricing.

caption: Rate from = the current Genesis PLR (6.825%) + the margin (−0.675%) = 6.15% a year
vo: So how's the rate worked out? Take the current Genesis PLR, six point eight two five percent, add the margin, minus zero point six seven five, and you get six point one five percent a year. The CRM calculates it, so nobody types it.

caption: The product sheet: features, eligibility, security & insurance
vo: Next, the product sheet itself. Features, eligibility, security and insurance, word for word what's on the Genesis website.

caption: Documents required, fees & charges and how to apply
vo: Then documents required, fees and charges, and how to apply. Exactly what Priya needs on a call.

caption: Docs tab: the document checklist for applications for this product
vo: The Docs tab holds the checklist. Every new application gets this list on its own Docs tab, showing what's in and what's still missing.

caption: Funds have the same product sheet
vo: Funds have the same kind of sheet. Here's the Income Fund.

caption: Business unit Funds, category Funds, risk rating on a 1–5 scale
vo: Business unit Funds, category Funds, and a risk rating from one to five. That rating is checked against the client's risk profile when they invest.

caption: No PLR margin, so no "Rate from": that applies to loans only
vo: There's no PLR margin here, so no Rate from. That's for loans only. Fund prices live in Investment Funds.

caption: Its applications use the "Fund subscription" checklist
vo: And its applications use the Fund subscription checklist.

caption: Product terms change: the CRM administrator updates the sheet
vo: Now, product terms change. When they do, the CRM administrator updates the sheet. Nobody else can edit the catalogue.

caption: Sign in as Kevin Lam — CRM Administrator
vo: So we sign in as Kevin Lam, the CRM administrator. Keeping the catalogue up to date is Kevin's job.

caption: Edit opens the product form
vo: Edit opens the product form, with every field on the sheet.

caption: Rate from stays greyed: it is calculated, never typed
vo: Rate from is still greyed. Change the margin, and it follows.

caption: Update Fees & charges with the new arrangement fee
vo: Kevin types the new arrangement fee into Fees and charges.

caption: Save: the change is recorded in the product's Audit tab
vo: Save, and the change goes straight into the product's audit trail.

caption: Everyone now sees the new fee on the product sheet
vo: And now everyone sees the new fee, including the RMs answering clients.

caption: The Audit tab shows the change: who made it and when
vo: The Audit tab shows who made the change and when, with the old and new values kept.

caption: Masters ▸ Genesis PLR History: the prime lending rate in force
vo: Where does the PLR come from? Masters, then Genesis PLR History. Every loan product reads the latest rate already in effect.

caption: When ALCO changes the PLR, the administrator adds a row: rate, effective date, approver
vo: When ALCO changes the PLR, the administrator adds a row, with the rate, effective date and approver. Every loan's Rate from recalculates at once. A future date simply waits for its day.

caption: Running loans are repriced through Loan Servicing ▸ PLR Change Campaigns
vo: Running loans are repriced through PLR Change Campaigns, in Loan Servicing. We won't change the PLR today, the demo loans rely on it.

caption: Masters ▸ Website Product Routing: which business unit and queue receives an enquiry
vo: Next door, Website Product Routing decides which business unit and queue receives an enquiry. One rule per product.

caption: Real Estate Loan enquiries go to Lending, queue Retail Loans
vo: Real Estate Loan enquiries go to Lending, in the Retail Loans queue, with a first contact target of four business hours.

caption: The website shows the catalogue straight from the CRM
vo: Now let's see it from the outside. The public website shows the catalogue straight from the CRM, no sign-in needed.

caption: The prime lending rate comes from the PLR History
vo: This prime lending rate comes from the PLR History. Exchange rates and fund prices do too.

caption: Products & services: one card per active product, with its legal entity
vo: Down here, one card per active product, each with its legal entity. Pick a category to narrow it down.

caption: Rates from 6.15% p.a.: the same Rate from as in the CRM
vo: Rates from six point one five percent a year, same as the CRM. Change the PLR or the margin, and the website follows.

caption: "Request more information" opens the enquiry form for this product
vo: A prospect clicks Request more information. The link carries the product code with it.

caption: The form opens with Real Estate Loan already chosen
vo: So the form opens with Real Estate Loan already chosen. All the prospect adds is what they need and how to reach them.

caption: Step 2: who is asking
vo: Step two is who's asking. Name, email, mobile and consent.

caption: Sent: the enquiry is created in the CRM and routed by the product
vo: Sent. The enquiry's created in the CRM, and routed by the product. Nobody re-types a thing.

caption: Back in the CRM, the enquiry is already in Enquiries & Leads
vo: Back in the CRM, it's already sitting in Enquiries and Leads, routed by Website Product Routing.

caption: Kavya Ramphul: Real Estate Loan, MUR 6,500,000 over 240 months
vo: Kavya Ramphul wants a Real Estate Loan, six point five million Mauritian rupees over two hundred and forty months. Kavya never had to pick the product, the link did.

caption: Business unit Lending and queue Retail Loans come from the routing rule
vo: Lending and the Retail Loans queue come from the routing rule, and a loans executive gets it automatically.

caption: The indicative rate is the same PLR + margin as Rate from
vo: The indicative rate is the same PLR plus margin as Rate from, and the instalment follows from it.

caption: Products & Services
vo: So, one product sheet drives what staff say, what applications need and what the website shows. Next up, Clients and Client 360.
